answer:
Analyze a solid circular shaft under pure torsion using small-deformation, linear-elastic relations.
The shaft is fixed at x = 0, has total length L = 1200 mm, and uniform diameter d = 30 mm.
The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76,923.1 MPa.
All calculations use the N-mm-MPa unit system.
Two external torques are applied: T1 = +200,000 N·mm at x = 1200 mm and T2 = −200,000 N·mm at x = 400 mm.
No transverse shear forces or bending moments act on the shaft; the problem is pure torsion only.
State the governing relations explicitly: polar moment of inertia J = πd⁴/32, maximum shear stress τ_max = T·c/J where c = d/2, and angle of twist per segment φ = T·L_seg/(J·G).
Compute the reaction torque at the fixed end (x = 0) from global equilibrium of the entire shaft.
Construct the internal torque diagram by cutting the shaft in each segment (0 to 400 mm and 400 to 1200 mm) and applying torsional equilibrium on a free-body diagram.
Report the internal torque value in each segment.
Compute the maximum shear stress at the outer surface in each segment; identify the segment and location where τ_max occurs.
Compute the angle of twist in each segment and sum them to obtain the total angle of twist of the free end (x = 1200 mm) relative to the fixed end (x = 0).
State all assumptions used, including: the shaft is prismatic (constant cross-section along its length), the material is homogeneous and isotropic, deformations are small, the cross-sections remain plane and perpendicular to the axis, and the stress-strain relation is linear (τ = G·γ).
Present all intermediate numerical values (J, c, segment torques, segment stresses, segment twists) before reporting the final results.
